translations.text: In the first year of Cyrus, king of the Persians, to fulfil the word of the Lord spoken by the prophet Jeremiah, the Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus, king of the Persians. He issued a command throughout his whole kingdom and wrote to everyone in these words:
"Thus says Cyrus, king of the Persians: The Lord, the God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and he has charged me to see to it that I build him a temple in Jerusalem, in Judea.
If there is anyone among you, among all the people of the Lord, with whom his God is, let him go up with him to Jerusalem in Judea and build the house of the Lord God of Israel.

And may God himself, who dwells in Jerusalem, be with him. Let him take all his provisions with him to the place where God himself dwells. And let him also take all his goods, whatever there is of gold and silver. Let him take other vessels and livestock with his companions, to furnish the temple of God in Jerusalem."

Then the heads of the ancestral houses of Judah and Benjamin rose up, together with the priests, the Levites, and everyone whose spirit the Lord God had stirred to go up and build the temple of the Lord in Jerusalem.
And all who lived around them helped and strengthened them. They put gold and silver, vessels and livestock into their hands, and filled them with gifts and offerings.

King Cyrus also had all the vessels used in the service of the house of the Lord brought out. King Nebuchadnezzar had carried these off from Jerusalem and placed them for safekeeping in the house of his own god.
Cyrus, king of the Persians, had all of them brought out by the hand of Mithridates [?], and he handed them over and gave them to Sanabassar, the governor of Judah.
And this is the number of the inventory: thirty gold sacrificial vessels, and one thousand and twenty-nine silver sacrificial vessels for the services,
thirty gold platters, and also a thousand silver ones.
All the vessels of gold and silver came to five thousand four hundred in all. They were brought from Babylon to Jerusalem with Sanabassar.

These are the people, each from his own place, who came out of the captivity. Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, had carried them captive to Babylon, and Cyrus brought them back from Babylon to Jerusalem in Judea, each man to his own city.
They came out with Zerubbabel, together with Jeshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Zrieliah, Mordecai, Balaasan, Masaphar, Gaguvar [?], Rehum, and Baanah. This is the number of the congregation of Israel:
the descendants of Parosh, two thousand one hundred and seventy-two;
the descendants of Shephatiah, four hundred and seventy-two;
the descendants of Arah, seven hundred and seventy-six;
the descendants of Lephthalem the Moabite [?], with the descendants of Jeshua and of Joab, two thousand eight hundred and twelve;
the descendants of Elam, two thousand two hundred and fifty-four;
the descendants of Zattu, nine hundred and twenty-five;
the descendants of Chorbe, seven hundred and fifty;
the descendants of Bani, six hundred and forty-eight;
the descendants of Bebai, six hundred and twenty-three;
the descendants of Azgad, three thousand three hundred and twenty-two;
the descendants of Adonikam, six hundred and sixty-seven;
the descendants of Bigvai, two thousand six hundred and six;
The sons of Adin: four hundred and fifty-four.
The sons of Ater of Hezekiah: ninety-two.
The sons of Bezai: three hundred and twenty-three.
The sons of Jorah: one hundred and thirty-two.
The sons of Hashum: two hundred and twenty-three.
The sons of Gibbar: ninety-four.
The sons of Bethlehem: one hundred and twenty-two.
The sons of Netophah: fifty-six.
The sons of Anathoth: one hundred and twenty-eight.
The sons of Azmaveth: forty-two.
The sons of Kiriath-jearim, Chephirah and Beeroth: seven hundred and forty-three.
The sons of Zaram and of Geba: six hundred and twenty-one.
The sons of Michmas: one hundred and twenty-two.
The sons of Bethel and of Iedea: four hundred and twenty-three.
The sons of Nebo: one hundred and fifty-two.
The sons of Magbish: one hundred and fifty-six.
The sons of Elamar: one thousand two hundred and fifty-four.
The sons of Aram: three hundred and twenty.
The sons of Liddon, that is, Lod, Hadid and Ono: seven hundred and twenty-five.
The sons of Jericho: three hundred and forty-five.
The sons of Senaah: three thousand six hundred and thirty.
And the sons of the priests: the sons of Eddo, of the house of Judah, of Jeshua [?]: nine hundred and seventy-three.
The sons of Immer: one thousand and fifty-two.
The sons of Pashhur: one thousand two hundred and forty-seven.
The sons of Erem: one thousand seven hundred.
And the Levites: the sons of Jeshua and of Kadmiel son of Judias, seventy-four.
And those who were psalm-singers and chanters, the sons of Asaph: one hundred twenty-eight.
The sons of the gatekeepers: the sons of Elom, the sons of Elumias, the sons of Atter, the sons of Talmon, the sons of Akkub, the sons of Hatita, the sons of Shobai. In all, one hundred twenty-eight.
And of the seed of Nathan: the sons of Suval, the sons of Asuphas, the sons of Tabaoth,
the sons of Keraos, the sons of Sea, the sons of Phadon,
the sons of Laban, the sons of Gaban, the sons of Jacob,
the sons of Abab, the sons of Selam, the sons of Anan,
the sons of Egdad, the sons of Gaar, the sons of Herad,
the sons of Herasun, the sons of Gazaam, the sons of Nikodan,
the sons of Asai, the sons of Phase, the sons of Baas,
the sons of Asai, the sons of Monim, the sons of Nephusim,
the sons of Gasuth, the sons of Akuphas, the sons of Aruras,
the sons of Bavluth, the sons of Midas, the sons of Arisas,
the sons of Bakur, the sons of Sisaras, the sons of Maan,
the sons of Nesovas, the sons of Attophas,
the sons of the servants of Solomon: the sons of Sotias, the sons of Asupherath, the sons of Phadduras,
the sons of Ielas, the sons of Kerdon, the sons of Keddiel,
the sons of Saphatias, the sons of Attil, the sons of Phakerath-Sabum, the sons of Iemei.
All the sons of Nathan and the sons of the servants of Solomon: three hundred ninety-two.
And these are the ones who came out of Telmelek, Laresa, Kerob, Edar and Meher. They could not give the names of their fathers, or show whether their family was from Israel.
The sons of Dazas, the sons of Tobias, the sons of Nekodas: six hundred fifty-two.
And of the sons of the priests: the sons of Abai, the sons of Akos, the sons of Berzelli. Because he took one of the daughters of Berzellos the Gileadite as his wife, their names were forgotten.
And they searched for the record of their family in their book, and it was not found, and they separated them from the priests. One thousand seven hundred fifty [?]. The prophet [?]
and he said to those families: "It is not lawful for you to eat of the holy thing of the holies until a high priest arises and reveals it openly, and through him all are fully enlightened."
And the whole assembly together was forty-two thousand three hundred sixty,
besides their male and female servants. And their shepherds were seven thousand and seventy-seven, and their singers (their psalm-singers), men and women, two hundred.
Their horses were seven hundred and thirty-six, and their mules two hundred and forty-five,
and their camels four hundred and thirty-five, and their donkeys six thousand seven hundred and twenty.
And the rulers, the heads of the fathers' houses, who came to the house of the Lord in Jerusalem, offered provisions to the house of God for building it,

as much as they were able, for building the house, into the treasury of the work: sixty thousand and ten thousand [?] drachmas of gold, five thousand talents of silver, and one hundred and fifty priestly tunics.
And the priests and the Levites and some of the people, and the singers and the gatekeepers and the Nethinim, settled in their own cities.
And the seventh [month] [?] came and arrived, and the children of Israel were each in his own city, and all the people gathered together as one man to Jerusalem.

And Jeshua son of Jozadak and his brothers the priests, and Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and his brothers, arose and built the altar of burnt offerings of the Lord God of Israel, to offer burnt offerings on it, as it is written in the law of Moses, the man of God.

And they set up the altar according to its proper arrangement, for they were afraid of the peoples of the land. And they offered burnt offerings on it at once to the Lord their God, one in the morning and one in the evening.
And they kept the Feast of Tabernacles, as it is written, and the burnt offering day by day in fixed number, as the Lord had commanded them.

And they also offered other burnt offerings: those of the new moons and of the sabbaths and of all the yearly feasts, holy offerings to the Lord, and of all the unblemished [?] who had sinned against the Lord [?].
And on the seventh [day] of the first month they began to offer burnt offerings to the Lord God. And the foundation of the house of the Lord had not yet been laid.

And he gave money to the stonecutters and the carpenters, and food and drink and oil to the Sidonians and the Tyrians, who were to bring cedar wood from Lebanon by sea to Joppa, as Cyrus king of Persia had commanded.

And in the second year of their coming, when they came to the temple of the Lord in Jerusalem, in the second month, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak and their brothers, the priests and the Levites, and all who had come from the captivity to Jerusalem, made a beginning. They appointed the Levites, from twenty years old and upward, as overseers over the work of the house of the Lord.

And Jeshua and his sons and his brothers, Kadmiel and his brothers, and the sons of Judah, were overseers over the work of the house of the Lord, along with the sons of Henadad, their sons and their brothers the Levites.

And they laid the foundation and began to build the house of the Lord. The priests stood clothed in their tunics and blew their trumpets, and the Levites, the sons of Asaph, blessed the Lord God with cymbals, as David king of Israel had ordained.

And each man said to his [?]: "Give thanks to the Lord and praise him, for he is good, for his mercy upon Israel is forever." And the whole assembly blessed the Lord with a loud voice, because the foundation of the house of the Lord had been laid.

And many of the priests and of the Levites, and of the rulers, the heads of the fathers' houses, and the elders, who had seen the house of the Lord and now saw its foundation with their own eyes, wept with a loud voice. And all the people made a show of joy and raised their voice.

And no one in the assembly could tell apart and hear the sound of their joy from the sound of the weeping, because of the great number. For the people were shouting with a loud voice, and the sound was heard in faraway places.
And those who were oppressing Judah and Benjamin heard that the sons of Israel had returned from captivity and were building the house of the Lord, the God of Israel.

And they came to Zerubbabel and to the rulers, the heads of the fathers' houses, and said to them: "Let us build with you, for like you we seek the Lord your God. We too have been offering sacrifices in this way from that day on, ever since Esarhaddon, king of Assyria, brought us here."

And Zerubbabel, Jeshua son of Jozadak, and the rest of the rulers, the heads of the fathers' houses of Israel, said to them: "It is not right for us and you to build the house of the Lord our God together. We ourselves will build the house of the Lord our God, as Cyrus, king of the Persians, commanded us."
And the people of that land weakened the hands of the assembly of Judea and kept them from building.
And they appointed adversaries and plotted to hinder them all the days of Cyrus, king of the Persians, until the days of Darius, king of the Persians.
In the reign of Ahasuerus over the Persians, at the beginning of his reign, they wrote a letter about those who lived in Judea and Jerusalem.
In the days of Artaxerxes, king of the Persians, the tax collector wrote a letter in Syriac, and it was translated.
Rehum, Baaltem, and Shimshai the scribe wrote a letter about Jerusalem to King Artaxerxes.

This was decided by Rehum, Baaltam, and Shimshai the scribe, and by the rest of our servants and kinsmen: the Dinaites, the Apharsathchites, the Tarpelites, the Apharsites, the Archevites, the Babylonians, the Susanchites, the Keeda [?], the Ueghe [?],
and the other remaining peoples whom the great and honorable Osnappar settled, and whom he settled in the land, in the city of Somoron, that is, Samaria, and the rest beyond the River.
These are the words of the letter that they sent: "To King Artaxerxes, from your servants, the men who live beyond the River.

Now let it be known to you, O king, that these Jews who came here from you to us have gone into the city of Jerusalem, the rebellious and provoking city. They are building it even now; they want to raise its walls, and they are raising up its foundations.
And now let it be known to you, O king, that if this city is built and its walls are raised, no one will pay you tribute, and they will become raiders against the kings.
And so they will rise up against the kings as [?] and raiders, and we do not wish to see this. And because of all this we have written to you, O king,

so that you may look and search in the book of records of your fathers. You will find there and understand that this city is a rebellious city, that it has always risen up against kings, and that its people have been a refuge for all fugitives at all times, forever. For this reason this city was laid waste.
Now we inform you, the king, that if this city is rebuilt and its walls are raised up, you will have no peace."
And the king wrote to Rehum Baltem and Shimshai the scribe, and to the rest of their servants and kinsmen who lived in Samaria and to the others beyond the river: "Peace be with you." And he said:
"These tax collectors whom you sent to me came before me
and made everything known to me. I made inquiry and found that from ancient times that city has been rebellious and has attacked all kings.

Mighty and fierce kings have dwelt in Jerusalem. They grew strong and seized the whole land to the west, beyond the river Euphrates. Now lay tribute and tax upon them, so that they may not again grow insolent through presumption [?].
Now I inform you: go and stop them and hinder that work of theirs, so that they do not build that city of theirs.
Do not pardon them or let them off. Take it to heart and exact from them all their tribute and tax, so that they do not multiply, grow strong and rise up to attack the great kings."

At that time the tax collector of King Artasast, that is, Artaxerxes, took the letter and read it aloud before Rehum and Sai the scribe and their servants and kinsmen. And they went up quickly to Jerusalem and to Judea with great force and with cavalry.

And they stopped the people and kept them from building. Having been hindered at that time, the work on the temple of God in Jerusalem stood idle. And it remained idle until the second year of Darius, king of the Persians.
And Haggai and Zechariah son of Iddo prophesied. They prophesied over Judea and Jerusalem, the house of the God of Israel.
At that time Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak arose and began to build the house of the Lord God in Jerusalem. The prophets of God were of one accord with them and helped them.

At that time Tattenai, the governor of the region beyond the river Euphrates, came to them with Shethar-bozenai and their servants and kinsmen, and they said to them: "Who commanded you to build this house, or by whose word have you raised up these towers?
Or what are the names of these men who are leading the building of this city?"
But the eyes of the Lord were upon the Jews who had returned from captivity, and they did not stop them until they could inform King Darius. And then they sent the tax collector about this matter,

so that they might know the contents of the letter that Tattenai, the governor of the region beyond the river, and Shethar-bozenai and their kinsmen, and the Apharsachites of the region beyond the river, sent to King Darius.
Reisim [?] sent them to him, and this is what was written to King Darius: "Abundant peace to you!

Let it be known to the king that we went to the land of Judea, to the city of Jerusalem, and we saw the temple of the great Lord God. They were building it with choice stones and setting timbers into its walls as covering [?]. The work was going forward and prospering in their hands.
Then we questioned their elders and said to them: "Who ordered you to build this house, or on whose word did you set it up?"
We also asked them the names of the men who were their leaders, so that we could inform you of this, and so that we could write down for you the names of the men and of their chiefs.

The Jews gave us this answer, saying to us: "We are servants of the Lord God of heaven and earth, and we are building the house as it was built many years ago, the house that the great king of Israel, Solomon, built. We too are setting this one up like that house.

"For our fathers angered the God of heaven and earth, and he gave them into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar, king of the Babylonians and the Chaldeans. He laid waste this house, and the people served Babylon.
"Then in the first year of Cyrus, king of the Babylonians, King Cyrus ordered that this house of the Lord God be built.

"Nebuchadnezzar had carried off the silver and gold vessels of the house of the Lord God from Jerusalem, and had come and brought them to the houses of his own gods. King Cyrus took those vessels out of the royal house and gave them to Sheshbazzar, the governor [?].
"He said to him: 'Take up all the vessels of service and bring them to the house of the Lord God that is in Jerusalem. Bring these vessels to their own place.'
"At that time Sheshbazzar came and laid the foundation of the house of the Lord God in Jerusalem. We have been building it from then until now, and we have not yet finished it.

"Now, if it seems right to you, the king, have a search made. Look in the houses and repositories of the record books of the kings of Babylon, so that you may find out whether King Cyrus really did order the building of the house of the Lord in Judea and Jerusalem. And when you, O king, have learned the facts of this matter, write to us."
Then King Darius had a search made, and it was found in the house of the chronicles, the records of the Babylonians.
In Iamathia [Ecbatana?], the city of the Batanaeans [?], he found one roll [?], a scroll, and this is what was written in that book of records:

"In the first year of King Cyrus, King Cyrus gave a command concerning the house of the Lord that is in Jerusalem. He said: 'Let the temple of the Lord be built, and a place where they may offer the offering of the Lord.' He set its measurements: sixty cubits high and sixty cubits wide,
with three courses of strong stones and one course of timber. 'Let the whole temple be built and joined together in this way.'

"Nebuchadnezzar carried off the gold and silver vessels of the house of the Lord from that house of the Lord in Jerusalem, and placed them in Babylon. Now give them back and bring them to the place, to the temple of the Lord in Jerusalem. Go and bring them to their own place, the house of God.

"Now give a letter of command to the governor of the province Beyond the River, Sathrabuzanes, and to his associates, the Apharsachites of the province Beyond the River, and further to those of the distant places [?].
"From now on, leave the building of that house of God to the leaders, the Jews and the elders of Israel. Build that house of God on its own site."

"And I have commanded that no one should hinder the elders of Judea any longer from building the house of the Lord their God. Under the authority of my reign, let those who collect tribute in the regions beyond the river give these men what they need, with all diligence, and let them not hinder them."

"Young bulls and rams, yearlings for burnt offering to the Lord God of heaven, and wheat, salt, wine and oil, as the chief priests of Jerusalem instruct you: let these be given to them day by day without hindrance, as they receive them."
"And offer a fragrant sacrifice to the Lord God of heaven, and pray for the life of the king and of his son."

"This command has gone out from me: if any man opposes my command, tear down his house, take a beam from his house, set that beam up, and nail to it the man who opposed my command. Let it be a reproach to him forever."

"And may God, whose name dwells there, destroy and overthrow any kingdom or people that grows bold and raises its hand to hinder and ruin that house of the Lord God which is in Jerusalem. I, King Darius, have issued this command; let no one have authority to transgress it."
At that time the governor of the region beyond the river, and Shethar-bozenai, and their fellow servants, to whom King Darius had written, quickly carried out his command.

And the elders of the Jews and the Levites were building, in the time of the prophesying of Haggai and of Zechariah son of Iddo. They built and completed it according to the command of the Lord God of Israel, and as King Cyrus and Darius had commanded, and in the times of Artaxerxes, king of the Persians.
On the third day of the month of Adar, in the sixth year of the reign of Darius, in the month of Mehrakan, the temple of God was completed.
And the sons of Israel, the priests and the Levites and those who had come out of the captivity, held the dedication of the house of the Lord with great joy.

At the dedication of the house of the Lord they offered a hundred calves, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs, and twelve yearling goats for the sins of all Israel, matching the number of the tribes of Israel.
And they appointed the priests, each to his own place, and the Levites according to their divisions, for the service of the Lord God in Jerusalem, as it is written in the book of Moses.
And the sons of Israel who had come out of the captivity kept the Passover of the Lord on the fourteenth day of the first month.

And the priests and the Levites purified themselves, and all of them were pure. They sacrificed the Passover of the Lord for all who had come out of the captivity, for their brothers and for the priests.

And the sons of Israel who had come out of the captivity ate the Passover. So did all those who had separated themselves from the uncleanness of the peoples of the land and had come to join them in seeking the Lord God of Israel.

And they kept the feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days and rejoiced greatly. The Lord had made them joyful and had turned the heart of the king of the Assyrians toward them, so that he would help them and strengthen their hands for the work of the temple of the Lord God of Israel.
And after these events, in the reign of Artaxerxes, king of the Persians, Ezra came up. He was the son of Seraiah, son of Azariah, son of Hilkiah,
son of Shallum, son of Zadok, son of Ahitub,
son of Amariah, son of Ezra, son of Sathiol [?],
son of Zerahiah, son of Uzzi, son of Bukki,
son of Abishua, son of Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron, the first priest.

This Ezra came up from Babylon. He was a scribe skilled in the law of Moses, which the Lord, the God of Israel, had given. And the king gave him everything he wanted and asked for, because the hand of the Lord his God was with him.

And some of the sons of Israel came up to Jerusalem with him, along with some of the priests and Levites, some of the singers, servants and gatekeepers, and some of the temple servants (Nethinim). Ezra left Babylon on the first day of the first month, and on the first day of the fifteenth [?] he entered Jerusalem, in the seventh year of King Artaxerxes.
He came up to Jerusalem in the fifth month, which was in the seventh year of the king,
and on the first day of the fifth month Ezra came to Jerusalem, because the hand of the Lord God was lifted up with him.
And Ezra set his heart on studying the law of the Lord, on writing it down, and on teaching Israel its commandments and judgments.
And this is the year [?] of the decree that King Artaxerxes gave to Ezra, the priest and scribe of the books, and of the words of the Lord, and of the commandments that concerned Jerusalem:
"Artaxerxes, king of kings, to Ezra, scribe of the law of the Lord, the God of heaven, with all firmness:
I have given a command concerning all those in my kingdom from the people of Israel, from the priests and the Levites, that all of them may go up to Jerusalem with you.
On behalf of the king and the seven counselors a letter has been written for an inquiry into the affairs of the Jews under the leadership of Ezra, who has the law of God in his hands.
And the king, together with his counselors, has ordered that silver and gold for the house of the Lord be taken to Jerusalem and placed in the temple before the Lord, the God of Israel.

And all the silver and gold that can be found, which the Jews were carried off [?] with into exile in Babylon, the people together with the priests are to take and bring to the house of God in Jerusalem.
And all who go out are to prepare these things in the manner we have written: calves, rams and lambs, and offerings and their gifts. Offer them on the altar of the Lord your God in Jerusalem.
And above all, I have done a kindness to you and your brothers and have left you gold and silver. Do with it as pleases your Lord.
And take with you the vessels given to you for the service of the house of the Lord, and hand them over to the house of the Lord in Jerusalem.
And give the rest to be kept in the treasury of the royal house.
I, King Artaxerxes, have commanded all the treasurers beyond the Euphrates River to give everything that Ezra, priest and scribe of the law of the Lord, the God of heaven, asks of you,
and to have ready a hundred talents of silver, a hundred measures of wheat, the same of wine, and the same measure of oil. And let no one resist the king's command.

Everything that I have commanded concerning the house of the Lord, the God of heaven, let it be done so. And let no one lift a hand to hinder the house of the Lord, the God of Israel, so that the wrath of God may not come upon my kingdom and my son's.

And we make known to you that none of those who are priests, Levites, psalm-singers, gatekeepers, or temple servants (Nethinim), who have been servants of the house of the Lord, shall pay tribute, and no one shall have authority to enslave them.

And you, Ezra, according to the wisdom of your God which is in your hands, appoint scribes and judges over them, so that they may judge all the people who are on the other side of the river and teach the law of your Lord to all who do not know it.

And all who do not act according to the law of the Lord and according to the king's command shall be handed over to punishment according to their deeds, whether death, or torture, or a fine, or imprisonment." At that time Ezra spoke thus:
"Blessed is the Lord, the God of our fathers, who put this into the heart of the king, that he should glorify the house of the Lord God which is in Jerusalem,

and he showed mercy to me and made me honored before the king and his counselors and before all the king's princes. And I took courage, for the hand of the Lord was fully raised up with me, and I gathered all the chiefs of Israel who had come out with me.
And these are the leaders of the heads of fathers' houses who came out with me in the reign of King Artaxerxes, the king of the Babylonians:
Of the sons of Phinehas, Gershom; of the sons of Ithamar, Daniel; of the sons of David, Hattush;
and of the sons of Zechariah, and of the sons of Parosh, Zechariah, and with him a hundred and fifty men;
of the sons of Pahath-moab, Eliana [Eliehoenai], son of Zerahiah, and with him two hundred men;
and of the sons of Zattu, Shecaniah, son of Jahaziel, and with them three hundred men;
and of the sons of Adin, Obed, son of Jonathan, and with him fifty men;
and of the sons of Elam, Jeshaiah, son of Athaliah, and with him seventy men.
And of the sons of Shephatiah, Zebadiah, son of Michael, and with him seventy men;
and of the sons [of ?], Joabadiah, son of Jehiel, and with him two hundred and twelve men;
and of the sons of Bani, Shelomith, son of Josiphiah, and with him a hundred and sixty men;
and of the sons of Bebai, Zechariah, son of Bebai, and with him twenty-eight men;
and of the sons of Adonikam and of Azgad, Johanan, son of Hakkatan, and with him a hundred and ten men;
and of the sons of Adonikam, the last ones. And these are the names of all of them: Eliphelet, Jeiel, and Shemaiah, and with him sixty men;
and of the sons of Bigvai, Uthai and Zabbud, and with him sixty men.

And I gathered them at the bank of the river that flows to Ieve [Ahava?], and we encamped there for three days; and among the multitude of the people I found no one of the sons of the priests or of the sons of the Levites.
And I sent for Eliezer and Ariel and Shemaiah, Aonaam [?], and Jarib and Zepanathan [?] and Zechariah and Meshullam and Joarib and Elnathan,

And pay attention: they will bring them before the princes who were in the place of Mephaseth [Casiphia?], and I will put words in their mouth, so that they may speak to their brothers, the Nethinim, who are in the place of Mephaseth, who brought to us those who would minister [?] in the house of our God, in the temple of the Lord.
And they came to us, for the hand of our God was with us always to exalt us, from the sons of the Levites and from the sons of Israel; and first there came to us his sons and his brothers, eighteen;
and Hashabiah and Jeshaiah, of the sons of Merari, and his brothers and his sons, twenty men.
And of the Nethinim, whom David and the princes gave for service, to attend the Levites: Nethinim, two hundred and twenty. And all of them were gathered according to their names.
And there, at the bank of the river Ahava, we proclaimed a fast, and we prayed before the Lord our God, and asked of him a straight way for us and for our children and for all that was with us.

For we were ashamed to ask the king for the help of horsemen to save us from our enemies on the road. We had said to the king thus: "The hand of the Lord our God is a helper to all who seek him in goodness, and his might and his wrath are upon all who have forsaken him."
And we fasted and asked God concerning all this of ours. And he heard us.
And we sent twelve of the chiefs of the priests: Sherebiah and Hashabiah, and with them ten of their brothers.
And we weighed out and gave them the silver and the gold, the first [?] service vessels of our God, with which the king and his counselors and all Israel who were there together had exalted us.
And I weighed out and gave them: silver, six hundred and fifty talents; and silver vessels, a hundred; and of gold, a hundred talents;
and gold vessels, twenty-three; and vessels of bronze, holy, choice, gilded.
And I said to them: "You too are sanctified by the Lord God, and all the vessels are holy to the Lord, of gold and of silver, set apart as a chosen offering for the Lord God of our fathers.

Be watchful and keep guard until you weigh them out before the princes, the priests and the Levites and the rulers, the patriarchs of Israel, who are in Jerusalem, in the chambers of the house of the Lord."
And the priests and the Levites took up the counted amount of gold and silver and vessels, and brought them to Jerusalem, into the house of our God.

And we arose and set out from the river Ahava on the twelfth day of the month [?], and we came and arrived at Jerusalem, by the hand of our God, which was with us; and he delivered us from the hands of our enemies and from our assailants who were on the road.
And we came to Jerusalem and rested there only three days.

And on the fourth day we weighed out and gave the silver and the gold and the vessels in the house of our God into the hands of Meremoth son of Uriah the priest; and with him was Eleazar son of Phinehas, and Jozabad son of Jeshua, and Noadiah son of Binnui, and other Levites.
And the whole number was counted, and all of it was written down to match the full number.

At that time those who had come out of captivity, the children of the exile, offered sacrifices to the Lord God of Israel: twelve bulls for all Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, and twelve yearlings for sins. They offered all these sacrifices to the Lord God.

They handed over the written list of the vessels, as the king had commanded, to his officials who served the king and to the governors of the region beside the river Euphrates. And they honoured the people and the temple of God.

When all this was finished, the leaders came to me and said: “The people of Israel, the priests and the Levites have not kept themselves apart from the people and the land, the nations that are set apart from them: the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, the Amorites, the Moabites, the Egyptians and the Movsiurites [?].”

“They have taken wives from among their daughters, both for themselves and for their sons [?], and the seed of their holiness has been mixed with the people of the land and defiled. This lawlessness began with the leaders.”
When I heard these words, I tore my garment, pulled out the hair of my head and my beard, and sat down in mourning.
Then everyone who feared the God of Israel gathered around me, all who had been assembled after coming out of exile. And I went on sitting in mourning until the time of the evening sacrifice.
At the evening offering I rose from my grief. With my garment torn, I was sorrowful and bowed on my knees, and I stretched out and lifted up my hands to the Lord my God.

I said: “My Lord and God, we are ashamed and afraid before you. Raise up my face toward you, my God [?], for our iniquities have multiplied above our heads, and our sins have grown great and risen up to heaven.

From the years and times of our fathers until this very day we have been in great sins. Because of our sins you handed us over, together with our kings and our children, into the hands of the kings of the Gentiles, to the sword, to captivity and to plunder, and we have been in the shame of our faces until this very day.

But now your mercies have been upon us, O Lord our God. You have granted us life, established us in the place of your sanctuary, and enlightened the eyes of our hearts, O Lord our God. You have given your salvation to us sinners, to each one of us in our servitude.

For we were enslaved, but in our servitude you did not abandon us, O Lord our God. You turned your mercies toward us in the sight of the king of the Persians, so that he gave us your salvation, raised up and rebuilt this desolate wilderness, and walled in the stronghold [?] of Judah and Jerusalem.
And now, what shall we answer before you, O Lord our God, for all this? For we have broken your law, O Lord our God, and your commandment,

which you gave us by the hand of your servants the prophets, and you said thus: "The land which you are entering to possess is a land defiled with the defilement of the peoples of that land, and they have filled that land with their uncleanness.

And now do not take any of their daughters as a wife for your son, and do not give your daughters as wives to their sons, and do not seek to make peace with them at any time. And be strong to eat the richness of that land, and you will make your children inherit that land for all time."
And what has befallen us has come because of our deeds and the wickedness of our sins; but you, O Lord God, have forgiven our sins many times and have given us such a seed and root.

And then we turned aside and transgressed your law and mingled with the filthy uncleanness of the peoples of that land; yet you were not angry with us to destroy us until now, until there would remain neither our strong one [?] nor our race, nor your severity [?] and your name upon us.

O Lord, God of Israel, you are righteous and true, and we have sinned against you; yet you did not wipe out our race from the earth, but a root and seed of our people has remained to this very day. Now, behold, we are before you today, O Lord, in our iniquities, and we can no longer stand before your face, for our iniquities and our wickednesses have multiplied more than the hairs of our head.

And when Ezra had worshipped with this confession, and lay fallen on the face of the ground with great lamentation before the temple of the Lord, all who were in Jerusalem gathered to him, a great multitude: fathers and mothers, young men and maidens; and the people lamented and raised the sound of their weeping.

And Jeconiah son of Eliah, of the sons of Elam, answered and said to Ezra: "We have sinned against the Lord our God, and have taken wives from the foreigners of that land. And now today there are iniquities in Israel, and great sin.

And now let us make a vow before our God to separate from every woman and from their offspring; and now, as you wish, arise and put fear into them by the law of the Lord our God, as the commandment orders.
Arise, and let us hear it from your mouth, and we are with you; be strong and act as it is commanded by the Lord our God."
And Ezra arose and made the chief fathers of the tribes of the priests and all Israel swear to act in this way, and they swore.

And Ezra rose and left the front of the house of the Lord and went to the treasure-house of Johanan son of Eliashib; he ate no bread and drank no water, and he mourned over their iniquities and over the multitude of their great sins.
And the herald proclaimed in Jerusalem and in Judea, and said:

"Everyone from among the rulers and the elders who does not come by the third day, let him be accursed together with all his possessions, and let him himself be cut off from the congregation of the people of Israel."

And every man of Judah and Benjamin gathered at Jerusalem within three days, in the ninth month, on the twentieth day of the month. All the people sat in the open square of the house of the Lord, and all of them were trembling because of his words and because of the winter cold.
And Ezra stood up and said to them: "You are the ones who have sinned and taken wives from the daughters of foreign peoples, and you have added lawlessness and sin to Israel.

So now give glory to the Lord, the God of our fathers, and do what is pleasing before him. Separate yourselves and withdraw from all the heathen of the land and from the foreign wives whom you have taken."
And the whole assembly answered and said: "This word that you have spoken against us is a great one,
for we are a numerous people, and it is the winter season, and we cannot stand outside. And this matter is not the work of one day or two days, for we have sinned greatly in this matter.

Let rulers be appointed in all places and cities, and let those who have foreign wives come at the time that the elders and the heads of families have set, city by city. Let them be judged, and let them remove this sin from us and turn away the wrath of God from us over this matter."
And Jonathan son of Asahel and Jahzeiah son of Tikvah were appointed over this matter, and Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levites assisted them.

And those who had come out of captivity did so. Ezra the priest chose for himself the men who were chiefs among the heads of families of his house, men of renown, and they came together on the first day of the tenth month and dealt with the matter.
And they separated every man who had a foreign wife, by the first day of the first month.
And among the sons of the priests were found some who had taken wives from foreigners: of the sons of Jeshua son of Jozadak and his brothers, Maaseiah and Eliezer, and Jarib and Gedaliah.
And they began to put away their foreign wives. And each of them offered rams for the sins they had committed in ignorance.
And of the sons of Immer: Hanani and Zebadiah.
And of the sons of Harim: Maaseiah, Selia, Shemaiah, Jehiel and Uzziah.
And of the sons of Pashhur: Elianas, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nathanael, Jehoshaphat and Elasah.
And of the sons of the Levites: Jozabad, Sam [?], Kolaiah (this is Akolitas), and Aphertias [?], and Judah and Eliezer.
And of the psalm-singers and chanters: Eliashib. And of the gatekeepers: Shallum, Telese [?] and Uri.
And of Israel, of the sons of Parosh: Hramiasel [?], Izziah, Malchijah, Eamim [?], Eleazar, Hashabiah and Nibanaiah [?].
And of the sons of Elam: Nattoniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Babdiah [?], Jeremoth and Elijah.
And of the sons of Zattu: Elioenai, Elishum [?], Mattanah, Jarmoth, Zabaath and Naziah [?].
And of the sons of Bebai: Johanan, Hananiah and Zabbai, and Othali.
And of the sons of Babine [?]: Meshullam, Malluch, Adaiah, Jasob [?], Sheal and Hremoth.
And of the sons of Pahath-moab: Adne, Chael [?], Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, Binnui and Manasseh.
And of the sons of Harim: Eliezer, Isshijah, Mechiah [?], Shemariah, Simeon,
Benjamin, Malluch and Shemariah.
And of the sons of Hashum: Mattenai, Mattattah, Lababath [?], Eliphelet, Jeremiah, Manasseh and Shimei.
And from among their sons, of the sons of Bani: Maadai, Amram, Uel,
Benaiah, Bedeiah, Cheluhi,
Vaniah, Meremoth, Eliashib,
Mattaniah, Mattenai,
and they did so, of the sons of Banui and of the sons of Shimei:
Shelemiah and Nathan, Adaiah,
Machnan, Gadu, Zesi, Aru,
Azarel, Shelemiah, Shemariah,
Shallum, Amariah, Joseph;
and from among them, of the sons of Nebo: Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Jaddai, Iadael, Joel, Benaiah.
All these were men who had taken foreign wives, and they had sons and daughters by them.
